descriptions.text: Standard Healing Potion. Increases your health by at least 50%. Doesn’t cure poison or other health-seeping conditions such as succubus-inflicted gonorrhea. So remember to wrap it up, bucko.

recap.text: Mordecai gives Carl a small red glass bottle with a cork, a third the size of a Coke bottle, and two bronze adventurer boxes then hold three more. With Donut soaked in blood, the Heal Critter scroll failing on her, and her potion countdown unknown after a mana potion, Carl tests on himself. He drinks one by hand, tasting kiwi juice, then a second before the fifteen-second timer ends, and the poison is nullified.

Crawler Sinjin of the fifteenth edition leaves a note in the Cookbook's explosives section: a level 3 sapper's table lets you infuse bombs, and a hobgoblin smoke curtain soaked in a healing potion and left to dry mass-kills undead like you wouldn't believe. Crawler Forkith of the twentieth confirms it. Bombs work too, but smoke works better, and high-level undead only get mad.

Mordecai suggests a trick before they leave: dip two potion balls in the red water of the Emberus shrine at the back of the room. The system labels the results Holy Goopers, a mix of blessed water, a fine healing potion and an air-activated coagulant. Emberus is a light-based god, so against vampires the mixture acts like napalm. Mordecai tells them to hit the vampires with it, then have Donut max out her Torch spell.

Carl levitates above a park several blocks wide, filled with red dots and roiling fog, and Sister Ines, who can tell whether a mob is undead, says every one of them is. He tosses a potion ball filled with a fine healing potion into a dense patch of red. Three of the mobs die, easily and soundlessly, for very little experience. Carl tells the others they are good to go.

Carl clenches his teeth and slips his new Legendary toe ring onto his left pinky toe, where it says twice that it must go. The ring stores one potion that triggers itself when his health meets a condition, and it prompts him to choose. He picks a gold-standard healing potion, set to trigger if his health reaches two percent.

beats.headline: A gift from Mordecai
beats.text: Mordecai produces a single glass bottle, small, about a third the size of a Coke bottle, red with a cork in it: a gift from him to Carl. Carl examines it, adds it to his inventory, which now has a Potions and Healing submenu, and pulls it back into his hand with a mental click. Put it on your hotlist, Mordecai tells him, and you will drink it without having to actually drink. Then his boxes open: one bronze adventurer box holds two more potions of healing, and another one more.
beats.gist: Mordecai gives Carl a small red corked bottle, and Carl stores it, then receives three potions.

beats.headline: Kiwi juice and poison
beats.text: Donut is soaked in blood and barely alive. The Heal Critter scroll will not work on her, and Carl does not know where her potion countdown stands: she took a mana potion a few minutes ago. So he tests on himself. The quick slots won't let him take a second potion. He drinks one by hand, his first time physically drinking one, and it tastes oddly like kiwi juice. Then he drinks a second before the fifteen-second timer is done. You have been poisoned! Poison effect nullified.
beats.gist: Donut is nearly dead, so Carl tests healing potions on himself, drinking a second before the timer ends.

Crawler Forkith of the twentieth confirms it. It works with bombs too, but smoke works better, and high-level undead only get mad.
